arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one original full-bleed reward picture for RevealLine's 1994 Forever theme; scenery revealed gradually during a game and enjoyed as a complete image after winning.
Format/composition: exactly one landscape 2:1 image, ideally 2048 by 1024 pixels. No panels or contact sheet. Rich full-scene composition with several readable discoveries across the width, a strong focal object and quieter connecting areas. Preserve broad light/dark shapes so partial reveals make intriguing fragments and the complete picture reads at phone size.
Style/medium: beautiful modern pixel-art illustration with the nostalgic visual language of late-1980s and early-1990s 16-bit adventure games; original art, not a reproduction of any game. Deliberate square pixel clusters, crisp stepped contours, restrained ordered dithering, carefully limited color families. Detailed architecture and tactile period objects without photorealistic texture, soft painted strokes, smooth vector gradients, 3D rendering or artificial CRT overlay.
Shared palette: deep ink navy, violet and petrol-blue shadows; warm amber and peach light; selective dusty-magenta and seafoam-cyan accents. Rich lighting expressed through clean stepped color clusters. Small luminous highlights should feel precious rather than covering every surface.
Constraints: No letters, words, digits, logos, brands, watermark or signature anywhere, including props, signs, packaging and screens. No HUD, menus, border, crosshair, gameplay line, score, or user interface. Any signs are blank colored panels; any decorative screen images are original simple abstract shapes. No existing film/game characters or copied artwork. No modern smartphones, flat-panel displays, LED billboards or modern vehicle styling. Opaque finished scenery fills the entire canvas.
Primary request: a warm, inviting late-night neighborhood arcade in 1994, viewed from just inside its open entrance at a low human-eye angle. A close row of chunky upright CRT arcade cabinets creates a strong diagonal into a small cozy room; one near cabinet's physical joystick, colored buttons and convex screen are the principal focal object. The screen contains only a few original abstract glowing geometric forms, with no text or familiar game. Beyond the cabinets, show tiled flooring, a plain empty stool and a glass entrance opening onto a quiet blue residential street with a bicycle and warm apartment windows. A dim back corner and reflective floor make the room feel deep, while localized cabinet glow paints cyan and rose patches on warm worn surfaces. No people are necessary. The picture should evoke the quiet last few minutes before going home, discovery and affection rather than a crowded futuristic cyberpunk megacity. Asymmetric intimate interior composition; emphasis on cabinet construction, glowing CRT glass, joystick silhouette and a glimpse of the neighborhood outside.

Primary request: an original 1989 neighborhood video-rental street on a rainy evening. Wide exterior composition viewed diagonally along the sidewalk from beneath the edge of a striped shop awning. A warmly lit compact rental shop window holds shelves of unbranded VHS cases with blank colored spines and a pair of small convex CRT television displays showing only original abstract color shapes. A single large VHS cassette and its plain partly open plastic case on the sheltered outside return counter provide a readable foreground focal prop. Their recognizable twin reel windows and ribbed plastic are carefully drawn without lettering. Rain-dark brick and pavement mirror broken amber, magenta and cyan light clusters. A parked era-appropriate boxy hatchback, a small tree, neighboring dark windows and a long ribbon of puddle reflections lead into the street. No people are necessary. Shop signs are blank illuminated panels without symbols that resemble writing. Quiet, tactile, cozy and rain-scented, with a different composition from an arcade interior. Keep the foreground cassette readable and wet reflections pixel-clustered, not blurry.

Primary request: a nostalgic 1992 train journey at dusk, seen from the seat of a modest passenger carriage through a large window as the train rests briefly beside a warmly lit small station. A close unbranded portable cassette player with a visible cassette-reel window, mechanical buttons and thin wired headphones rests on the window-side table and is the main foreground focal prop. No writing, logo or numbers on the player, cassette or station. Warm compartment lamplight catches scuffed plastic, the headphone wire and fabric upholstery. Outside, amber platform lamps recede along a quiet canopy toward a brick station building, with blue-violet evening tracks and distant tree silhouettes. Separate crisp near-object shapes from layered exterior depth; broad cool window space contrasts with the warm intimate foreground. No people are necessary. Make it feel like a remembered journey and the promise of arriving somewhere, not science fiction, an abandoned carriage or an advertisement. Strong close still-life-plus-landscape composition, distinct from both the arcade room and rainy shopping street.
